# Task: Hermetic fetch handling for relative CSV calls in happy-dom

**Parent:** AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12

## Summary

Close the escape route at the harness level: in the `integration` (happy-dom) project, a
relative `/api/csv/...` fetch must never reach a stray real server (whose root may be the
main checkout). Install a default fetch guard in `src/test/setup.ts` that refuses such
requests unless a test explicitly installs its own bridge, and document the pattern.

## User story

As a test author, I want an accidental un-bridged `/api/csv/...` call to fail loudly and
locally instead of silently PUTing into whichever server happens to answer
`http://localhost:3000`.

## Scope

- `src/test/setup.ts` (integration project only): install a default `fetch` wrapper that
  - passes non-`/api/csv/` requests through to the native fetch,
  - for `/api/csv/...` requests without an installed bridge, rejects (or returns a
    synthetic `503` with a clear message) naming the test file and pointing at the bridge
    helper, without performing any network I/O.
  - keeps `vi.stubGlobal('fetch', …)` bridges (used by `configStore.integration.test.ts`)
    working: the wrapper only applies when no per-test stub replaced the global.
- Add/centralise a small bridge helper (e.g. `src/test/csvFetchBridge.ts`) so a test opts in
  with one call, mirroring the existing `installFetchBridge` in
  `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts`.
- Add the documenting comment in the integration tests that exercise real saves: relative
  fetches resolve against the happy-dom origin, so every real save **must** install the
  bridge; note the `configStore` test-mode guard as the second line of defence.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Parent AC 4 (AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12) covered by this item:** **Escape route closed** — No test can PUT through a live dev-server endpoint by accident: relative `/api/csv/...` fetches in the happy-dom project must resolve against a test-controlled origin (explicit bridge/stub), never a stray `localhost` server that could answer from the main checkout. Add a comment in the integration tests documenting the relative-fetch/bridge pattern and verifying the bridge is installed for every real save.

- In the `integration` project, an un-bridged relative `/api/csv/...` fetch fails the test
  with a message naming the file and the bridge helper; no real network request is made
  (asserted with a native-fetch spy that must not be called).
- `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts` keeps passing with its explicit bridge and
  temp root; the bridge helper is reused rather than duplicated if that is a pure
  refactor.
- The guard is a no-op for non-CSV requests (e.g. telemetry upload, asset fetches) so no
  existing integration test regresses.
- A comment in the integration tests documents the relative-fetch/happy-dom origin hazard
  and the requirement to install the bridge for every real save.
- Full `integration` project suite passes via `/skill:test`.

## Key Files

- `src/test/setup.ts` — default fetch guard for `/api/csv/...`.
- `src/test/csvFetchBridge.ts` — shared bridge helper (new, small).
- `src/test/csvFetchBridge.test.ts` — unit tests for the guard/helper.
- `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts` — reuse the helper, add the documenting comment.
- `vitest.config.ts` — reference only (`setupFiles: ['src/test/setup.ts']`).

## Minimal implementation (smallest end-to-end slice)

1. Write the guard helper + unit tests (un-bridged rejection, bridged pass-through,
   non-CSV pass-through).
2. Wire it into `src/test/setup.ts` for the integration project.
3. Reuse it in `configStore.integration.test.ts` and add the documenting comment.
4. Run the changed-scope suite via `/skill:test` to confirm no integration regressions.

## Notes / risks

- `vi.stubGlobal`/`vi.unstubAllGlobals` ordering matters: if the default guard is installed
  at module scope it must be re-installed after `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` in `afterEach`;
  document the resolution in the helper.
- Do not simply hard-stub `fetch` globally — that would break legit non-CSV fetches in
  scene/telemetry tests.
- Overlap: this item is complementary to the `configStore` test-mode guard (which prevents
  the fetch from being issued at all); both are required by the parent ACs.
data.title: Task: Hermetic fetch handling for relative CSV calls in happy-dom

requirement, and the suite-run tracked-CSV guard. Update the existing docs entries that
describe the CSV endpoints and the config store save path so they match the new behaviour.

apply to, so a future change does not reintroduce a cross-checkout CSV write.

## Goal

Drive the sortie-long warble from the shared pass so it starts at spawn and stops on every terminal, identically in the game and the gyms (parent AC1).

User story: As a player, I want to hear the classic UFO warble for the drone's whole sortie so I always know it is out there farming for me.

## Scope

- Start the warble exactly once at spawn in the shared spawn path (`spawnDrone`); stop it at every terminal: return-leg begin, payout/teardown, and destruction.
- Use the drone's phase-transition surface (`MysteryUfoDrone`) + `tickDrones` removal/teardown in `CombatCoreScene` so the same code runs in game and gyms (shared core only, gym-parity rule).
- Tests through the fixture recorder: start exactly once at spawn; stop called on return-leg begin, on payout, on destruction (incl. mid-sortie) and on teardown; no start/stop mismatch on repeated ticks; extend the cue contract with a stop-on-all-terminals assertion.

- `src/scenes/core/combatDrone.ts`
- `src/entities/MysteryUfoDrone.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`
- `src/audio/effects.ts`

Parent AC1 — warble lifecycle: a classic "woo-woo-woo" UFO warble cue plays continuously from spawn through the seek and collect phases (the whole sortie) and stops when the drone begins its return leg, pays out, is destroyed, or is torn down — delivered as a start/stop continuous cue with control companions (mirroring `stopDiveSound`/`stopThrusterSound`), at a level-appropriate audible gain that respects the shared SFX volume/mute settings.

The spill already exists (`hitDrone`/`scatterMineralDrops`) — nothing is double-spawned, only voiced/visualised.

# Enriched scenario registry schema and resolver

## Summary

Extend the shared dev-scenario registry and resolver so an entry can carry
**promo metadata** — bot-tuning preset name, promo level reference, optional
deterministic seed, and the editorial categories it evidences — resolved into
a new `kind: 'promo'` union member, while the existing `boss` / `defeat`
entries keep their exact behaviour. This is the scaffolding slice (AC1, AC5):
the first promo entries and wave definitions arrive in later siblings.

## Requirements & context

- Single source of truth stays `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs` (plain ESM
  importable by bare Node and Vite); types live in
  `scripts/capture-scenarios.d.mts` and must not leak `any` into `src`.
- `src/core/devScenario.ts` already derives its supported names from the
  registry and fails fast on drift — extend, don't loosen, that contract.
- Dev-only gating (`import.meta.env.DEV`) is unchanged: production never
  honours the `scenario` parameter (AC1).
- Editorial category vocabulary comes from `EDITORIAL_CONFIG` in
  `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` (`weapons`, `pickups`, `enemies`, `boss`).

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs` — richer entry schema + promo entries
- `scripts/capture-scenarios.d.mts` — updated types
- `src/core/devScenario.ts` — `kind: 'promo'` resolution + docs
- `scripts/capture-scenarios.test.ts` — contract tests (sibling test-first)

## Deliverables

- Optional promo metadata on registry entries (backward-compatible shape).
- `DevScenario` union extended with a `kind: 'promo'` member carrying
  `preset`, `promoLevel`, optional `seed` and `categories`.
- Updated `.d.mts` type declarations, resolver branch, and doc comments.

## Dependencies

- Prereq: `Promo scenario contract tests (test-first)` — the suite this
  feature turns green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (schema):** `CAPTURE_SCENARIOS` entries carry optional extra fields
  (`preset`, `promoLevel`, `seed`, `categories`) and the existing three
  entries remain unchanged in name, effect and runtime behaviour (AC1).
- **AC2 (types):** `scripts/capture-scenarios.d.mts` declares the richer
  shape with no `any` leaks; src consumers compile cleanly (AC5).
- **AC3 (resolve):** `resolveDevScenario` maps a registered promo URL to
  `{ kind: 'promo', … }` and returns `null` for unknown/invalid values; a
  promo value not registered fails fast at module load (AC1/AC5).
- **AC4 (gating):** Production builds ignore the promo parameter exactly as
  today's scenarios do (AC1).
- **AC5 (suite):** The test-first contract suite and the full existing suite
  pass with this change (AC5/AC7).

## Appendix note

Designed from the parent intake brief (Q1–Q3 answered 2026-10-27); no new
questions required.

# Curated bot-tuning presets for promo scenarios

## Summary

Add a small set of **named bot-tuning presets** to `src/data/bot-tuning.json`
(which today holds only `Default`) so promo scenarios can vary the bot's
personality — e.g. aggressive hunter, cautious collector, evasive, glass
cannon — via the existing preset store, with **no new ShipConfig rows** (the
producer's Q1 answer on AH-0MVI5XI73000ZVYA). The presets are sparse
overrides: `coerceTuningValues` fills every unspecified key from defaults, so
the file stays small and readable.

## Requirements & context

- Existing store (`src/core/botTuningStore.ts`) already exposes
  `getBotTuningConfig(name)` and the fallback chain
  localStorage → bundled baseline → built-in `Default`; this slice adds data
  plus tests, not a new store.
- Watch Demo (and demo-mode capture) selects the current preset; promo
  scenarios select a preset **by name** at run start (parent AC2).
- Presets must be meaningfully distinct (different emphasis/priority
  spikes) so footage varies across scenarios (AC3's range).

**Key Files:**
- `src/data/bot-tuning.json` — new named presets (sparse overrides)
- `src/data/bot-tuning.test.ts` — preset validity/distinctness/no-invalid-key
  tests
- `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` — read-only reference (lookup path)

## Deliverables

- ≥4 curated named presets in the bundled JSON, each documented one-liner.
- Hermetic tests: preset lookup, fallback chain unchanged, referenced presets
  exist, presets differ in ≥1 meaningful tuning key.

## Dependencies

- Prereq: `Enriched scenario registry schema and resolver` — the
  preset-name contract and `CAPTURE_SCENARIOS` the cross-check test reads.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (presets):** `src/data/bot-tuning.json` ships ≥4 named presets (in
  addition to `Default`), each authored as sparse overrides that
  `coerceTuningValues` completes deterministically (AC2).
- **AC2 (cross-check):** A hermetic test asserts every `preset` referenced by
  a registered promo scenario exists in the bundled state, and that each
  preset differs from `Default` in ≥1 documented tuning key (AC2/AC5).
- **AC3 (store):** `getBotTuningConfig(name)` returns each new preset and the
  existing fallback chain (localStorage → bundled → Default) is unchanged —
  no regression in `botTuningStore` / bundled-config tests (AC2).
- **AC4 (suite):** The full existing suite passes with the new data (AC7).

## Appendix note

Designed from the parent intake brief (Q1–Q3 answered 2026-10-27); no new
questions required.

# Promo wave definitions module

## Summary

Add a new **dependency-free promo-scenario data module** holding
hand-authored, `LevelDefinition`-compatible wave definitions for the promo
catalogue (the producer's Q2 answer on AH-0MVI5XI73000ZVYA: hand-author all
new promo-tailored waves). Content is composed **only** from the existing
spawner/movement archetypes (V/diver swarm, centipede, ghost, harvester,
horde, strike, lane traffic, asteroid, mini-boss, boss) — no new gameplay
behaviour, so the gym↔game parity and duplicate-body guards stay quiet.

## Requirements & context

- Plain ESM data (like `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs`): importable by bare
  Node (capture CLI) and the Vite build with types via a `.d.mts`.
- Each promo level is deterministic for a given seed and maps to ≥1 of the
  four editorial categories (`weapons`, `pickups`, `enemies`, `boss`) via
  per-wave metadata, consumed by the catalogue tests later.
- Waves must be bot-survivable and sustain watchable action; the calibration
  slice (sibling `Calibrate bot survival and 45-second footage`) tunes them
  afterwards — this slice delivers the structure and the validation seam.

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/promo-scenarios.mjs` — hand-authored promo level definitions
- `scripts/promo-scenarios.d.mts` — types for the data
- `scripts/promo-scenarios.test.ts` — hermetic validation tests

## Deliverables

- Promo level data module with exported levels, per-level category metadata
  and seed determinism contract.
- Validation tests: wave-group shape (WaveManager's validator), archetype
  whitelist, determinism per seed, plain-ESM importability.

## Dependencies

- Prereq: `Enriched scenario registry schema and resolver` (data shape + how
  promo level references resolve).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (content):** `scripts/promo-scenarios.mjs` exports ≥1
  `LevelDefinition`-compatible promo level per planned catalogue entry, built
  only from existing archetypes/flags — nothing new dynamically spawned
  outside the existing spawner classes (AC2).
- **AC2 (validation):** Hermetic tests run `WaveManager`'s wave-group
  validation over every promo wave, assert the archetype whitelist (no new
  movement class), and prove no duplicate-body guard or gym↔game parity test
  is triggered (AC2/AC5).
- **AC3 (determinism):** Each promo level is a pure function of its seed —
  the same seed yields identical waves; the test asserts this (AC2).
- **AC4 (categories):** Every promo level declares ≥1 editorial category key
  from `EDITORIAL_CONFIG`, and the module is readable by the compile-promo
  category vocabulary (AC3).
- **AC5 (portability):** The module imports cleanly in bare Node and in the
  Vite build (mirroring the registry parity pattern) (AC2).

## Appendix note

Designed from the parent intake brief (Q1–Q3 answered 2026-10-27); no new
questions required.

# Apply promo scenarios in PlayScene bot-flight

## Summary

Wire the promo scenario through the game at run start: a `kind: 'promo'`
dev scenario forces **demo/bot mode** (the Watch Demo bot pilots), injects
the scenario's hand-authored promo level as the run campaign, applies the
scenario's bot-tuning **preset by name**, and seeds the run from the
scenario's seed — all through existing seams only, dev-gated exactly like
today's scenarios (AC1/AC2/AC5).

## Requirements & context

- `PlayScene.create()` already resolves and applies dev scenarios via
  `_applyDevScenarioFromUrl()` (line ~1100); the promo path must be applied
  **before** `_applyBotTuning()` (line ~955) and `waveManager.beginGame()`
  (line ~1077) so the preset and campaign are live from frame one — resolve
  the URL early in `create()`/`init` and let the normal campaign block prefer
  the scenario's promo level.
- Promo runs are **bot-flown** (parent AC2): the scene must set
  `demoMode`-equivalent flight when a promo scenario is active so
  `getBotInput()` supplies bot input — without requiring a human pilot.
- The existing `boss` / `defeat` scenarios keep their freeze/release behaviour
  unchanged (backward compatibility).
- Campaign injection reuses `waveManager.setLevels(...)`; preset application
  reuses `getBotTuningConfig(name)` + the `toCompetentOverrides` /
  `toHumanOverrides` mapping already used by `_applyBotTuning`.

**Key Files:**
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — promo application seam at run start
- `src/core/devScenario.ts` — `kind: 'promo'` union member + URL resolution
- `src/scenes/PromoScenario.integration.test.ts` — new bot-flight integration
  test (mirrors `demoMode.integration.test.ts`)
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — read-only reference (injected campaign)

## Deliverables

- Early URL resolution + promo application in `PlayScene` (campaign, preset,
  seed, bot flight).
- Integration/demo check proving a promo scenario is bot-flown with the
  injected campaign and preset.
- Documentation comments on the new seams.

## Dependencies

- Prereq: `Curated bot-tuning presets for promo scenarios` (preset lookup).
- Prereq: `Promo wave definitions module` (promo level data).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (apply):** A `kind: 'promo'` dev scenario starts a run that flies the
  Watch Demo bot, plays the scenario's promo level as the campaign, applies
  the scenario's preset by name, and seeds the RNG from the scenario's seed —
  all present in the first frame (AC2).
- **AC2 (gating):** The promo path is inert in production builds and when no
  promo scenario is requested; normal runs and the existing boss/defeat
  scenarios are byte-for-byte unchanged (AC1).
- **AC3 (integration):** The integration/demo check (new or existing
  demo-mode suite) asserts bot input is honoured, `getBotTuningConfigName()`
  reports the scenario's preset, and the run is seeded deterministically —
  AC5's demo check.
- **AC4 (parity):** Gym↔game parity and duplicate-body guards stay green; no
  new gameplay behaviour is introduced (parity constraint).

## Appendix note

Design decision recorded for the producer: promo scenarios imply bot flight
and therefore force demo-mode flight when active (dev-only). Consistent with
parent AC2 ("bot-pilotable end to end"). No new questions required.

# Calibrate bot survival and 45-second footage

## Summary

Prove — and where needed tune — that the competent bot survives and keeps
producing watchable action for **≥45 s** in every promo scenario before the
demo game-over dwell, using the existing headless AI eval harness rather than
ad-hoc browser captures (AC2's sustained-footage target).

## Requirements & context

- The repo already ships `src/ai/eval/` (`arena.ts`, `engine.ts`) which builds
  the **real campaign** through `buildSequencedLevels` — the same harness can
  fly the competent bot against an injected promo level headlessly.
- A scenario the bot dies in instantly is a wasted clip; a flat set of similar
  archetypes reads as repetitive (parent's recorded risks).
- Calibration knobs are wave composition/count/timing (promo wave data) and
  preset tuning (bot-tuning.json) — **not** new gameplay behaviour.
- Any evidence-gathering long run must follow the shared background-job
  etiquette (launch → prepare → one completion-aware wait).

**Key Files:**
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — read-only harness reference for the check
- `scripts/promo-scenarios.mjs` — wave tuning target
- `src/data/bot-tuning.json` — preset tuning target
- `src/waves/promoScenario.survival.test.ts` — new hermetic survival check

## Deliverables

- A hermetic (no browser) per-scenario survival/duration check with an
  explicit ≥45 s assertion and bounded runtime.
- Tuned wave/preset data so every scenario passes.
- Recorded evidence (measured durations) in the completion comment.

## Dependencies

- Prereq: `Author 10+ promo scenarios by editorial category` (the catalogue
  being measured).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (harness):** A hermetic test/script drives the competent bot over each
  promo level via the existing eval harness and reports per-scenario simulated
  action duration before game over (AC2).
- **AC2 (threshold):** Every promo scenario sustains ≥45 s of action before
  the demo game-over dwell; failures name the scenario and measured duration
  (AC2).
- **AC3 (tuning):** Any scenario below threshold is fixed by tuning wave
  composition and/or preset values only — no new spawner behaviour, and the
  gym↔game parity/duplicate-body guards stay green (AC2).
- **AC4 (regression):** The check runs in bounded time as part of the standard
  suite and the full existing suite passes (AC5/AC7).

## Appendix note

Designed from the parent intake brief (Q1–Q3 answered 2026-10-27); no new
questions required.

# Fail fast on unwritable --out and invalid tune CSV

## Goal (user story)
As a developer running tune-loop verification I want `--tune` to validate `--out` (and the
balance CSV path) before anything expensive starts, so an invalid path fails in seconds with
an actionable message instead of running both sweeps first and then hanging or dying.

## Problem
`scripts/evaluate.mjs` only touches the output directory after both batches have run:
`executeTune()` calls `mkdirSync(options.outputDir, {recursive: true})` *after* the candidate
sweep (line ~394) and `main()` does the same for the non-tune path (line ~441). The 2026-10-21
negative probe (`--out /proc/nope/x`, 2 games x 200 ticks) therefore ran both sweeps and then
stalled for 166.6 minutes before an external SIGKILL (parent item AH-0MVIKLOOJ0058Z9B).

## Expected behaviour
- `node scripts/evaluate.mjs --tune --set enemy-configs.csv boss.health=7 --games 2 --ticks 200 --out <unwritable>`
  exits non-zero in well under two seconds, printing a single clear diagnostic on stderr.
- The probe runs **before** `loadCore()` (no Vite SSR boot) and before any `--tune` sweep.
- The `--tune` CSV target (`src/data/<tuneFile>`) is validated up-front too: a missing or
  unreadable CSV fails fast with its own message instead of failing after a baseline sweep.

## Implementation sketch (smallest end-to-end slice)
1. Add an exported, unit-testable probe to `scripts/evaluate.mjs`, e.g.
   `ensureWritableOutputDir(dir)` → `{ok: true}` | `{ok: false, code, message}`:
   `mkdirSync(dir, {recursive: true})`, then write + `fsync` + unlink a sentinel file
   (`.evaluate-write-probe-<pid>`) so an unwritable-but-existing directory (`EACCES`) is
   caught, not just a non-creatable one (`ENOTDIR`, `EROFS`).
2. Export a matching `assertTuneInputs(csvPath)` (`readFileSync` probe) for the `--tune` CSV.
3. In `main()`, call the probes immediately after `parseEvaluateArgs`/`--help` handling and
   **before** `loadCore()`; on failure write `output directory not writable: <dir> (<code>)`
   (and the CSV equivalent) to stderr and return a non-zero exit code (2 — same class as the
   existing usage-error exit, documented in `EVALUATE_USAGE`).
4. Keep the late `mkdirSync` calls as a cheap idempotent safety net; do not duplicate the
   validity logic.
5. Update `EVALUATE_USAGE` and `docs/BALANCING.md` (§Tuning loop → "Guards and guarantees")
   with the fail-fast validation, and extend the doc guard
   (`src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts`) to assert the new statements.

## Key Files
- scripts/evaluate.mjs
- scripts/evaluate-failfast.test.ts
- scripts/evaluate-args.test.ts
- docs/BALANCING.md
- src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The repro command fails fast (< 2 s) with a clear "output directory not writable" diagnostic and a non-zero exit, demonstrated after the fix (timings quoted in a work-item comment).
2. The writeability probe and CSV-path validation run before loadCore() and before any baseline or candidate sweep, proven by a test that observes no SSR boot on the failure path.
3. An unwritable-but-existing directory (EACCES) and a non-directory path (ENOTDIR) both fail fast, and the --tune CSV path is validated before the baseline sweep.
4. --tune with a valid --out still runs baseline -> edit -> re-run -> compare -> restore and exits 0; existing behaviour is preserved and existing evaluate/tune tests stay green.
5. CLI help (EVALUATE_USAGE) and docs/BALANCING.md mention the new validation, and the docs-guard test asserts it.
6. Unit tests cover the writeability probe and the CLI exit codes for each failure path, run under the project test policy (test skill).

Discovered-from: AH-0MVIKLOOJ0058Z9B
Depends-on: slice 1 (repro + red tests)

# Journal the tune CSV edit so a hard kill cannot leave it dirty

## Goal (user story)
As a developer I want the tune/edit cycle crash-safe, so that even an external SIGKILL, OOM or
timeout kill of the CLI never leaves `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` edited in the worktree — or,
if it does, the very next invocation (or a documented one-line command) restores it exactly.

## Problem
`executeTune()` applies the edit through `applyCsvEditFile()` and restores it in a `finally`
via `restoreCsvFile()` using the in-memory `attempt.originalText`. A SIGKILL runs no `finally`,
so the edited CSV survives the process (observed on 2026-10-21 immediately after the exit-137
kill, parent item AH-0MVIKLOOJ0058Z9B).

## Expected behaviour
- Before the first edited byte is written, a small journal (target path + original bytes) is
  persisted beside the CSV and fsynced.
- The journal is git-ignored, so a crashed run never shows up as a worktree change.
- After a successful restore (or with `--keep-edit`) the journal is removed.
- Any subsequent `scripts/evaluate.mjs --tune` invocation that finds a stale journal first
  reconciles it (restores the original bytes, removes the journal, prints a warning) and then
  proceeds — so no manual step is needed in the normal case.
- A documented manual repair path exists for the case where the CSV must be restored without
  running the CLI again.

## Implementation sketch (smallest end-to-end slice)
1. New module `scripts/csvEditJournal.mjs`:
   `writeJournal(csvPath, originalBytes)` — write `<csvPath>.tune-journal` (JSON: csvPath,
   base64 original, pid, ISO timestamp) to a temp name, `fsync`, `rename` (atomic);
   `readJournal(path)`; `clearJournal(path)`; `reconcileJournal(path)` — restore original
   bytes when the journal exists, then delete it, returning `{action: 'restored'|'none'}`.
2. Wire into `executeTune()`: write the journal before `applyCsvEditFile`'s write, and clear
   it inside the existing `finally` after `restoreCsvFile()` resolves.
3. `main()` reconciles a stale journal for the `--tune` target before validation proceeds.
4. Add the journal pattern to `.gitignore` (e.g. `src/data/*.tune-journal`).
5. Document the guarantee + repair commands in `docs/BALANCING.md` (§Tuning loop →
   "Guards and guarantees"), and assert it in `src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts`.

## Key Files
- scripts/evaluate.mjs
- scripts/csvEditJournal.mjs
- scripts/evaluate-failfast.test.ts
- scripts/csvEdit-shell.test.ts
- src/utils/csvEdit.ts
- docs/BALANCING.md
- scripts/evaluate-args.test.ts

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A simulated hard kill (SIGKILL) after the edit leaves a journal; the next invocation restores the CSV byte-identical to the pre-run state, verified by a test that kills a child process and compares bytes.
2. The journal is written (fsynced, atomically renamed) beside the CSV before the edited bytes are written, and is removed after a successful restore or when --keep-edit is used.
3. The journal path is git-ignored so a crashed run leaves no worktree change, asserted by a .gitignore guard test.
4. A deterministic, documented repair path restores the CSV exactly, documented in docs/BALANCING.md together with the journal file name.
5. Unit tests cover the journal write, restore-from-journal and stale-journal reconciliation, run under the project test policy (test skill).
6. Existing tune behaviour is preserved: --tune with a valid --out still runs baseline -> edit -> re-run -> compare -> restore, exits 0, and existing evaluate/tune tests stay green.

# Per-run progress output and opt-in sweep watchdog

## Goal (user story)
As a developer (or an agent) running a long tune sweep I want visible per-run progress and an
opt-in bounded-runtime guard, so an abnormal run can never stall silently for hours and so a
timeout aborts cleanly with the CSV already restored.

## Problem
`--tune` prints nothing between start and the final summary: `executeTune()` runs two
`runBalanceBatch()` sweeps with no output. When the 2026-10-21 negative probe stalled, the only
signal was a silent process for 166.6 minutes until an external SIGKILL (parent item
AH-0MVIKLOOJ0058Z9B). After slice 2 the known hang is gone, but a future stall in the sweep
itself (configuration-driven blow-up, non-determinism guard loop, I/O stall) would again be
invisible.

## Expected behaviour
- Every `--tune` run writes one progress line per completed game to **stderr**:
  `[tune] baseline 1/2 seed=1 policy=competent`, then `[tune] candidate 2/2 …`, then the phase
  transitions (edit applied, comparing, restoring). Stdout stays byte-identical to today so
  artifact/print parity and determinism are preserved.
- `--watchdog <seconds>` (default `0` = off) arms a bounded-runtime guard: on expiry the run
  prints a diagnostic naming the phase and the elapsed time, restores the CSV (journal from
  slice 3 + synchronous restore), and exits with a distinct code (124) rather than leaving a
  killed-but-dirty worktree.
- `--help` and `docs/BALANCING.md` document both.

## Implementation sketch (smallest end-to-end slice)
1. Reuse the existing per-run hook instead of adding a second mechanism: `runBatch` already
   accepts `config.onRun` (`src/ai/eval/engine.ts`), but `runBalanceBatch()` in
   `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` does not expose it (and `CliOptions.telemetrySink` is ignored there).
   Add an optional second parameter `runBalanceBatch(options, hooks?: {onRun?})` that forwards
   `onRun`; keep the existing signature/behaviour when `hooks` is omitted.
2. In `executeTune()`, pass an `onRun` that writes the progress line to `io.err` (count games
   against `sweep.seeds.length * policies.length`) — no divergent copy of the sweep logic.
3. Add `--watchdog <seconds>` parsing to `parseEvaluateArgs` (validated: finite, >= 0;
   non-numeric → usage error exit 2), arm a timer in `executeTune()` and clear it in the
   existing `finally`; on expiry: diagnostic + `restoreCsvFile` + `process.exitCode = 124`
   (use `exitCode`, not `exit()`, so pending stderr drains and the pipe cannot mask the exit).
4. Docs: `docs/BALANCING.md` tune flags table + "Guards and guarantees"; assert in
   `src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts`.

## Risky assumptions
- A watchdog timer inside a synchronous sweep cannot interrupt a *blocking* synchronous call —
  it only fires between runs. Recorded as an accepted limitation: the guard catches stalls that
  yield to the event loop (the observed case is caught by slice 2's fail-fast path instead), and
  the progress lines remain the primary signal for a truly blocking stall. Document this
  limitation in `docs/BALANCING.md`.

## Key Files
- scripts/evaluate.mjs
- src/ai/eval/cli.ts
- src/ai/eval/engine.ts
- src/ai/eval/cli.test.ts
- scripts/evaluate-args.test.ts
- docs/BALANCING.md

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Every --tune run emits per-run progress lines on stderr (never stdout), covered by a unit test that captures both streams.
2. An opt-in bounded-runtime watchdog (--watchdog <seconds>) aborts the sweep with a clear diagnostic naming the stalled phase, restores the CSV, and exits with a distinct non-zero code, covered by a test.
3. The full verification command used in AH-0MVBNLM2V008XC8T (including the negative probe) completes without hanging, with elapsed times recorded in a work-item comment.
4. Progress wiring reuses the shared runBatch onRun hook through runBalanceBatch (no divergent sweep copy in the shell), covered by cli.test.ts.
5. Artifact/print parity is preserved: stdout and the four tune artifacts are byte-identical to the pre-change output for the same seed/options (determinism tests stay green).
6. --help and docs/BALANCING.md document --watchdog, its default (off), its exit code, and the accepted limitation that a blocking synchronous stall cannot be interrupted, asserted by the docs guard.

# Relax single-type test pins to identity-preserving

## Summary / user story

**As a designer**, I want the campaign's documented level identities expressed as *dominance* assertions rather than *purity* assertions, so the producer's Q2=a decision ("preserve the dominant archetype, add variety around it") can be implemented without deleting the intent those pins protect.

The current suite pins Level 1 to "scouts only" and Level 5's filler waves to "phasers only". Those pins encode the very repetition the parent item removes. This feature replaces each purity pin with an equivalent, stricter-where-it-matters identity pin **before** the data changes land, so the tests document the intended end state.

## Scope

- `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts` AC1 "Level 1 uses Scout V-formations with no enemy fire".
- `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts` AC1 Level 2 "mixed single-enemy waves" and Level 3 "mixed pairs" pins (keep the structural identity — one group per L2 wave, ≥2 archetypes per L3 wave — and relax only archetype purity).
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts` phaser-only filler pins for Level 5.
- `src/waves/campaignInvariants.test.ts` — keep dominant-style, authoring-mix, showcase and difficulty pins exactly as they are; change only assertions that assume single-type purity.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Level 1's pin asserts scout **dominance** (scouts present in every wave and the level's dominant archetype) plus its retained wave-1 Scout V-formation and the no-fire rule — not "scout is the only archetype".
2. Level 2's pin keeps the single-group-per-wave structure; Level 3's pin keeps ≥ 2 archetypes per wave; neither asserts archetype purity.
3. Level 5's pin asserts phaser dominance (phaser present in the majority of waves and dominant by spawned weight) instead of phaser-only composition.
4. Every relaxed assertion is accompanied by a UK-English code comment naming Q2=a on the parent item (AH-0MVI5XXOU00954EA) and explaining why purity was relaxed.
5. No assertion is deleted without a replacement of equal or stronger intent; `campaignInvariants.test.ts` showcase/mini-boss/ramp/fire-boundary assertions are unchanged.
6. Tests that were failing because of the future data change are re-expressed so they pass both before and after the data work (structural/identity assertions), or are explicitly marked pending with a recorded reason.


**Parent-AC traceability.** This item discharges the following acceptance criteria of the parent epic (AH-0MVI5XXOU00954EA), restated here so the link is explicit and auditable:
- **Parent AC3** — Each level keeps its dominant archetype identity (Level 1 Scout-dominant, Level 5 Phaser-dominant; classic-arcade levels keep their showcase archetypes), varying around it with secondary archetypes, verified by per-level dominant-archetype assertions and the GDD §3.2 identity text still holding.

## Minimal implementation

- Replace the `new Set(['scout'])` equality with a dominance + presence assertion helper.
- Reuse the dominant-archetype helper from `src/waves/campaignVariety.ts` (delivered by the audit feature) instead of duplicating weight logic in tests.
- Update the pin comments and record the rationale in this work item.

## Dependencies

- Requires the campaign-variety audit module (composition/dominance helpers, AC1–AC3 coverage).
- Must land **before** the Level 1/Level 5 pilot rework and the remaining levels' rework (test-first ordering).

## Deliverables

- Updated `WaveManager.test.ts`, `sequencedLevels.test.ts`, `campaignInvariants.test.ts` pins.
- Rationale comment on this work item.

**Key Files:**
- src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts
- src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts
- src/waves/campaignInvariants.test.ts
- src/waves/campaignVariety.ts

# Level 1 + Level 5 pilot: identity-preserving variety (vertical slice)

## Summary / user story

**As a player**, I want Level 1 and Level 5 to stop fielding one identical archetype for ten waves, while still feeling like "Entry" (scouts) and "Predictable Death" (phasers).

This is the **tracer-bullet** feature: the two hardest levels for the identity-vs-distinctness tension (the parent's highest risk) are reworked end-to-end — authored data, identity pins, campaign variety tests and code comments — before the remaining eight levels are touched. If the pattern works here, it is the template for the rest of the campaign.

## What to change

- `src/waves/Formations.ts` Level 1: scout-led waves with secondary archetypes introduced gradually (e.g. a diver or swarm escort appearing on alternating waves), keeping the gentle escalation, no enemy fire, and the wave-10 dense scout-phalanx mini-boss.
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` Level 5: phaser-led waves with secondary archetypes varying around them (e.g. tank/diver escorts alternating), keeping the memorisable crosshair-grid feel and the wave-10 phaser+tank mini-boss.
- No new archetypes; existing roster only.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Level 1: ten waves, ≥ 2 distinct archetypes across the level, **no adjacent pair sharing a composition**, scout dominant overall, `shootEnabled: false` on every wave, wave-10 `miniBoss: true` retained, wave 1 retains a Scout V-formation.
2. Level 5: ten waves, ≥ 2 distinct archetypes, **no adjacent pair sharing a composition**, phaser dominant overall, `shootEnabled: true`, wave-10 phaser+tank `miniBoss: true` retained.
3. The campaign-variety assertions **for Level 1 and Level 5 are activated and pass**; the level-scoped (not campaign-scoped) variants of the AC1/AC2 assertions are made green for both levels by this item, so no skip marker survives for L1/L5 once it lands.
4. If the campaign-wide aggregate assertion is still red because Levels 2–4 and 6–10 have not been reworked yet, it stays explicitly skip-marked with a reason pointing at the pending rework items — never silently deleted or weakened.
5. Identity pins from the pin-relaxation item pass unchanged for both levels.
6. Level comments in `Formations.ts` explain the secondary-archetype pattern in UK English, naming the parent item and the Q2=a decision.

# Enforce sequential distinctness for generated waves

## Summary / user story

**As a player**, I want generational (`curve`/`dynamic`) waves to also change their enemy mix wave-to-wave, so the guarantee cannot be broken just because a wave is produced by the sequencer rather than hand-authored.

Parent AC1 applies to **all** modes (producer Q3=c'). Today only twelve waves are generated, but the sequencer minimises difficulty error with no concept of the previous wave, so a generated wave can legally repeat its predecessor's archetype set.

## What to change

Add a **sequential-distinctness constraint** to the shared generated-wave path:

- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`: accept an optional "avoid these archetype sets" input (e.g. `SequencerOptions.avoidCompositions`) and, when the error-minimising composition matches an avoided set, deterministically select the next-best eligible candidate/composition instead.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts`: track the previous wave's composition within a level and pass it in; `fixed` waves are never passed to the sequencer, so they remain exempt on the generated path (they are covered by authored data instead).
- `src/core/waveBalance.ts`: expose the composition signature / R4 distinctness rule as a named, documented rule beside R1–R3 so the sequencer and the campaign audit share one definition and one precedence order.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A generated wave never shares its archetype composition with the immediately preceding wave in the same level, across the shipped campaign at the default seed.
2. The constraint is deterministic: the same (curve, candidate pool, seed) always yields the identical campaign; no `Math.random`, no order-dependent iteration.
3. R1–R3 remain enforced and are audited over the rebuilt campaign; when distinctness and a balance rule conflict, **the balance rules win** and the resolution is documented next to the precedence.
4. Degenerate-input safety is preserved: an empty/one-entry candidate pool, or a level where no alternative composition exists, falls back to the best eligible composition rather than throwing or emitting an empty wave.
5. Target error is measured, not hidden: `campaignBalanceAudit` continues to report per-wave enforcement cost and the campaign stays inside the sequencer acceptance band; any wave that cannot satisfy distinctness within the band is recorded as follow-up authoring work rather than tolerated silently.
6. Unit tests cover: constraint satisfied; next-best fallback; no candidate left; `fixed` waves never constrained; `archetypeUsage` map not corrupted between waves.
7. No seeded-build regression: existing determinism and seed-divergence tests stay green.


**Parent-AC traceability.** This item discharges the following acceptance criteria of the parent epic (AH-0MVI5XXOU00954EA), restated here so the link is explicit and auditable:
- **Parent AC1** — No two sequential waves anywhere in the built campaign (Levels 1–10 × 10 waves, `buildSequencedLevels()` output) share the same enemy composition, verified by a unit/integration test asserting pairwise distinctness of adjacent waves across all 100 waves at default config, applying to `curve`, `dynamic` and `fixed` modes alike.
- **Parent AC4** — Generated (`curve`/`dynamic`) waves continue to satisfy the classification balance rules R1–R3 (opening formation-only, no all-chaser wave, bounded ranged mix), verified by the existing `waveBalance` audit/validator tests passing over the rebuilt campaign.
- **Parent AC6** — The same seed reproduces the same campaign; `curve`/`fixed` waves stay seed-independent and `dynamic` waves remain a pure function of (curve, candidate pool, seed), verified by seeded-build equality tests as in the opening-variety item (AH-0MUOCJM0N000RW2B).

## Minimal implementation

- Extend `SequencerOptions` with an optional avoided-composition set; compute candidate compositions from the already-evaluated greedy result.
- Pass the previous wave's composition from `buildConfiguredLevel` in `sequencedLevels.ts`.
- Add the shared composition/rule helper to `src/core/waveBalance.ts` and reuse it in the audit module.
- Add the unit tests and extend the campaign audit with a distinctness check.

## Dependencies

- Campaign variety audit (shared composition signature).
- Can proceed in parallel with the Level 1/Level 5 pilot; **must** complete before the campaign-wide verification item.

## Deliverables

- Sequencer option + builder wiring + shared rule constant.
- Unit and campaign tests proving the constraint and its precedence.
- Target-error record in the audit output.

**Key Files:**
- src/core/difficultySequencer.ts
- src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts
- src/core/waveBalance.ts
- src/waves/campaignBalanceAudit.test.ts
- src/core/difficultySequencer.variety.test.ts

# Authored variety rework — Levels 2–4 (onboarding)

## Summary / user story

**As a player**, I want every level of the 100-wave campaign to change its enemy mix from wave to wave, so a run never feels like ten repetitions of the same encounter.

This is the first half of the bulk data work: the hand-authored `fixed` waves of the no-fire onboarding levels 2–4 are re-mixed so **no two sequential waves share an archetype composition**, while each level keeps its documented identity (Q2=a), its showcase waves and its wave-10 mini-boss. Levels 6–10 are handled by the sibling classic-arcade/finale item (same file, so the two land serially to avoid conflicting edits).

## Scope

- `src/waves/Formations.ts` static `LEVELS` data for Levels 2, 3 and 4 (Levels 1 and 5 are delivered by the pilot item; Levels 6–10 by the sibling item).

1. For Levels 2, 3 and 4, **no adjacent wave pair shares an archetype composition**, verified through the shared audit module, and those level-scoped AC1 assertions are activated and green when this item lands (AC1 for this slice).

5. Levels 2–3 remain no-fire and Level 4 remains firing; the `targetDifficulty` rows for these levels stay non-decreasing and the AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K pins pass (AC5).

- **Parent AC1** — No two sequential waves anywhere in the built campaign (Levels 1–10 × 10 waves, `buildSequencedLevels()` output) share the same enemy composition, verified by a unit/integration test asserting pairwise distinctness of adjacent waves across all 100 waves at default config, applying to `curve`, `dynamic` and `fixed` modes alike.

- Run the audit module's per-level report after each level and record the result in a comment.

# Document and verify the fixed/curve/dynamic mode mix

## Summary / user story

**As a designer**, I want the per-wave generation mode ledger to be explicit and test-pinned, so it is clear which waves are hand-authored for identity/showcase and which are generated for per-run variety (producer Q3=c').

The parent adopts a **mixed** mechanism: authored `fixed` waves where a showcase/pin requires them, `curve` where determinism is wanted, and `dynamic` filler where seeded variety is safe. Today that mix is implicit in the CSV. This feature makes it a documented, verified contract, and converts a filler wave to `dynamic` **only** where the authored data cannot express the intent.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A documented per-wave mode ledger (a table covering all 100 waves: level, wave, mode, and the one-line reason it holds that mode) is published in the GDD's default-campaign note.
2. A test asserts the shipped CSV/config **matches** the ledger: all three modes are used, every recorded showcase/opening/mini-boss wave is `fixed` (or its curated opening mode), and no unlisted wave silently changes mode.
3. For every `dynamic` wave the seeded-determinism contract holds (same seed ⇒ identical campaign; different seeds may differ) and AC1/R1–R3 still hold across a multi-seed sweep.
4. If a filler wave is converted to `dynamic`, the ledger records the conversion plus its reason and the wave remains within the sequencer acceptance band; if no conversion is warranted, the ledger records that decision explicitly as a documented no-op.
5. `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` header comments and `src/core/configStore.ts` comments describe the final mix and link the ledger.
6. Any mode change keeps `shootEnabled` correct for the level (Levels 1–3 off, 4–10 on).

# Campaign variety regression, determinism and full-suite verification

## Summary / user story

**As a maintainer**, I want one verification item that proves the rebuilt 100-wave campaign is varied, deterministic, balanced and regression-free, so the epic can be reviewed against its acceptance criteria with evidence rather than assertion.

## Scope

Verification only — no behaviour changes unless a genuine defect is found (which becomes a linked follow-up work item).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 evidence**: a campaign-wide assertion confirms zero adjacent composition duplicates across all 100 waves in the built campaign at the default config and seed, and a multi-seed sweep (≥ 3 seeds) keeps AC1 holding for generated waves.
2. **AC2/AС3 evidence**: the per-level archetype-count (≥ 2) and dominant-archetype identity assertions pass for all ten levels, and the recorded report is attached to this work item.
3. **AC4 evidence**: R1–R3 hold for every generated wave over the shipped campaign and across the seed sweep; the balance audit's per-wave enforcement cost stays inside the sequencer acceptance band.
4. **AC5 evidence**: the non-decreasing target ramp, the Levels 1–3 no-fire / Levels 4–10 fire boundary, the ten-wave-per-level shape, and the wave-10 mini-boss encounters are all still pinned and green, including the AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K pins.
5. **AC6 evidence**: same-seed builds are byte-identical; `curve`/`fixed` waves are seed-independent; `dynamic` waves diverge across seeds. Determinism tests run over the rebuilt campaign.
6. **AC7 evidence**: the full project suite passes through the test skill; any failure is triaged into a critical `test-failure` work item with the blocking relationship recorded, and zero untriaged failures remain.
7. **Gym↔game parity evidence**: the campaign is built once in the shared core and consumed by `PlayScene` and the gyms — the parity assertions already in `src/waves/campaignBalanceAudit.test.ts` (AC3 gym↔game parity) and `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` stay green, and no divergent wave data copy is introduced.
8. The verification report (per-level archetype counts, adjacent-duplicate result, mode ledger snapshot, balance/target error summary) is recorded as a comment for audit.


**Parent-AC traceability.** This item discharges the following acceptance criteria of the parent epic (AH-0MVI5XXOU00954EA), restated here so the link is explicit and auditable:
- **Parent AC1** — No two sequential waves anywhere in the built campaign (Levels 1–10 × 10 waves, `buildSequencedLevels()` output) share the same enemy composition, verified by a unit/integration test asserting pairwise distinctness of adjacent waves across all 100 waves at default config, applying to `curve`, `dynamic` and `fixed` modes alike.
- **Parent AC2** — All 100 waves are in scope (not just the opening four); every level's wave list shows more than one enemy archetype across its ten waves, verified by a per-level archetype-count assertion ≥ 2 across the ten waves.
- **Parent AC3** — Each level keeps its dominant archetype identity (Level 1 Scout-dominant, Level 5 Phaser-dominant; classic-arcade levels keep their showcase archetypes), varying around it with secondary archetypes, verified by per-level dominant-archetype assertions and the GDD §3.2 identity text still holding.
- **Parent AC4** — Generated (`curve`/`dynamic`) waves continue to satisfy the classification balance rules R1–R3 (opening formation-only, no all-chaser wave, bounded ranged mix), verified by the existing `waveBalance` audit/validator tests passing over the rebuilt campaign.
- **Parent AC5** — The non-decreasing target difficulty, the Levels 1–3 no-fire / Levels 4–10 fire boundary and the wave-10 mini-boss encounters are unchanged, and the AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K regression pins pass, verified by the existing campaign regression and invariant suites.
- **Parent AC6** — The same seed reproduces the same campaign; `curve`/`fixed` waves stay seed-independent and `dynamic` waves remain a pure function of (curve, candidate pool, seed), verified by seeded-build equality tests as in the opening-variety item (AH-0MUOCJM0N000RW2B).
- **Parent AC7** — New or updated unit/integration tests cover sequential distinctness, per-level identity, determinism and regression, and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Minimal implementation

- Run the audit tooling over the built campaign; capture the report.
- Add/extend the seeded-build and determinism tests where coverage is missing.
- Run the full suite via the test skill and record the outcome.

## Dependencies

- Generated-wave distinctness.
- Authored variety rework — Levels 2–4 (onboarding).
- Authored variety rework — Levels 6–10 (classic-arcade + finale).
- Mode-mix ledger (its final state is part of the evidence).
- Pin relaxation.

## Deliverables

- Verification tests (where new coverage is needed).
- Verification report comment.
- Full-suite result recorded.

**Key Files:**
- src/waves/campaignVariety.test.ts
- src/waves/campaignInvariants.test.ts
- src/waves/campaignBalanceAudit.test.ts
- src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts
- src/core/difficultySequencer.variety.test.ts

**Parent:** AH-0MVIB7PD50029ZY1 — Background scenes (covers parent AC1: ≥ 20 bundled NASA photos with attribution/licence; feeds AC6 evidence).

## Goal

As a player I want each level's backdrop to be a real NASA space photograph, and as the producer I want every bundled image traceable to its source and licence, so the game ships redistributable art with no runtime dependency on NASA services.

## Background

Producer answer Q1 (2026-10-25): **bundle** the photos as committed repo assets and **record attribution and licence** per image. Today the repo has no image-asset pipeline at all: the only image is the MenuScene GitHub-logo data URI (`src/assets/github-mark.svg`) and audio assets live in `public/audio`. Network access to NASA's images API was verified available from this host on 2026-10-28 (`https://images-api.nasa.gov/search?q=nebula` → `200`), and `ffmpeg` is installed locally, so resizing needs no new dependency.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `public/assets/backgrounds/` contains **≥ 20** committed NASA space photographs whose filenames match the texture keys from `src/data/backgrounds.ts` one-to-one (no orphan files, no missing files); each image is ≤ 1920×1080, and the whole directory is ≤ 5 MB (report the measured total in the completion comment).
2. `public/assets/backgrounds/ATTRIBUTION.md` lists **every** image with: filename, NASA title/asset id, source URL, licence statement (US Government public-domain / NASA media-usage guidelines) and retrieval date; a per-image table with no gaps. The NASA media-usage URL is cited.
3. `src/data/backgrounds.assets.test.ts` (Node `fs`, no Phaser boot) enforces: file count ≥ 20, exact 1:1 key↔file match with the manifest, per-file and directory size budgets, image dimensions readable and ≤ 1920×1080 (JPEG/WebP header inspection or a tiny Node header parser — no new dependency), no byte-identical duplicate files, and an attribution row for every filename including a licence phrase.
4. No runtime NASA fetch: a test asserts no `nasa.gov`/`images-api` URL is reachable from `src/**` runtime code (documentation/attribution files and the dev-only fetch script are excluded), and the fetch/resize tooling lives outside the runtime entry graph.
5. `npm run build` (which includes `check-bundle-hygiene`) succeeds, and the assets are served from the built bundle (verified path: `dist/assets/backgrounds/…` or `dist/assets/…` depending on the chosen location, recorded in the completion comment).

6. **Parent-AC traceability:** this slice's primary implementation is parent AC #1 — "At least 20 NASA space photos are bundled as game assets (public-domain / NASA-approved media) with attribution and licence notes; backgrounds render at the full 960×540 canvas (Phaser FIT scaling) and are a non-interactive layer that never occludes gameplay or intercepts input." — specifically the bundling + attribution half; the full-canvas non-interactive render half is AH-0MVSEB7SA004B26C; the remaining ACs of this slice are the verification and the collateral work it needs.

## Minimal Implementation

- Write `src/data/backgrounds.assets.test.ts` first with placeholder expectations, then add the images until it is green.
- Dev-time only script `scripts/fetch-nasa-backgrounds.mjs`: query `https://images-api.nasa.gov`, download selected candidates into a temp dir, resize/compress with `ffmpeg` to ≤ 1920×1080 JPEG (quality ~80), emit `public/assets/backgrounds/<key>.jpg`. The script is tooling, never imported by `src/`.
- Curate for gameplay readability: dark, space-dominant, low-detail-in-the-middle images; reject anything that would fight the neon vector art.
- Write `ATTRIBUTION.md` from the metadata the script records (title/nasa_id/href/licence) so filenames cannot drift from attribution.
- Keep every asset under `public/assets/backgrounds/` (parent Key Files decision) so Phaser can load them by stable relative URL under Vite `base: './'`.

## Deliverables

- `public/assets/backgrounds/` — ≥ 20 compressed NASA photos.
- `public/assets/backgrounds/ATTRIBUTION.md` — per-image source/title/licence table.
- `scripts/fetch-nasa-backgrounds.mjs` — reproducible dev-time fetch/resize tooling.
- `src/data/backgrounds.assets.test.ts` — asset/attribution contract tests.

**Key Files:**

- `public/assets/backgrounds/ATTRIBUTION.md` — new directory holding the photos plus the attribution table.
- `public/assets/backgrounds/background-nebula-01.jpg` — one concrete example entry per bundled photo (≥ 20 files, keys from `src/data/backgrounds.ts`).
- `scripts/fetch-nasa-backgrounds.mjs` — new dev-only tooling.
- `src/data/backgrounds.assets.test.ts` — new asset contract tests.
- `src/data/backgrounds.ts` — texture keys / filename helper consumed by the tests (no edits expected unless the contract needs a helper).

## Dependencies

- Depends on: deterministic background manifest (texture keys + filename helper).
- Blocks: AH-0MVSEBW8L009O3JD (PlayScene level-change wiring needs the textures present for review).

**Parent:** AH-0MVIB7PD50029ZY1 — Background scenes (covers parent AC1 non-interactive full-canvas layer, AC4 readability dimming, AC5 shared-core parity).

## Goal

As a player I want a dimmed space photo behind the neon gameplay at every level, and as a developer I want the background's create/dim/swap/destroy lifecycle to exist **once** in the shared combat core, so `PlayScene` and the gyms render identical backdrops and nothing intercepts input or leaks across restarts.

## Background

`PlayScene.create()` currently draws an inline black rectangle at `PLAYSCENE_BACKGROUND_DEPTH = -1000` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`); `CombatScene` sets `backgroundColor: '#000000'` in its config block and `src/core/gameConfig.ts` uses `GAME_BACKGROUND_COLOR`. Gyms (`GymFormationScene`, `GymWeapons`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility` — all `CombatScene` subclasses) draw no backdrop of their own. AGENTS.md requires shared behaviour to live once in `src/scenes/core/` and forbids forked copies; the repo-wide duplicate-body guard (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) enforces that.

Texture availability is the key design constraint: scene tests boot through `src/test/gameHarness.ts` (happy-dom, stubbed rendering) and cannot decode real JPEGs, so the layer must (a) accept an injected texture — tests register fixtures — and (b) degrade to the existing solid `GAME_BACKGROUND_COLOR` backdrop when a key is absent, without stalling scene `create()`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. New `src/scenes/core/backgroundLayer.ts` owns the whole background lifecycle: create (image + dim overlay), `setLevel(level)` swap via `backgroundForLevel`, and `destroy()`; every tuning value (dim alpha/colour, nullable fallback colour, depth) is an exported constant — shared tuning lives in `src/core/constants.ts` — and no layering logic is duplicated in scenes.
2. Shared hooks on `CombatCoreScene` (`_createBackground()`, `_setBackgroundLevel(level)`, and teardown inside the existing `teardownRunState()`), so `PlayScene` and every `CombatScene` gym call the **same** code; `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (duplicate-body guard) passes with no allow-list additions.
3. The background renders full-canvas at 960×540 (`setOrigin(0)`, display size `GAME_WIDTH × GAME_HEIGHT`, `scrollFactor(0)`), sits at depth ≤ −1000 (below gameplay at 0 and the juice layers at −10…−7) and is **non-interactive**: no input handlers are attached and pointer/keyboard input reaches the gameplay layer — asserted by test during a live scene tick.
4. Readability: a dim overlay (exported alpha/tint) sits above the photo and below gameplay so enemies, bullets and the player stay legible; when no texture is available the layer renders the solid `GAME_BACKGROUND_COLOR` fallback instead (no throw, no repeated warning spam).
5. Missing-texture safety and no-stall guarantee: booting `PlayScene` (and one gym) in the test harness with **no** background textures registered completes `create()` and ticks without error, and a subsequent `setLevel()` with a registered fixture texture swaps to that texture — both tested.
6. `PlayScene` uses the shared layer instead of its inline black rectangle (initial level from `waveManager.level`), and the layer is destroyed on shutdown/restart so no display object survives into the next run — tested via the scene-restart path.

7. **Parent-AC traceability:** this slice's primary implementation is parent AC #4 — "Gameplay readability is preserved: backgrounds are dimmed/desaturated beneath the neon vector art so enemies, bullets and the player ship stay legible (GDD §7.1 aesthetic, "2.5× keeps bullets legible against the neon background")." — specifically the dimming/readability rule, plus the full-canvas non-interactive layer from parent AC #1 and the shared-core home from parent AC #5; the remaining ACs of this slice are the verification and the collateral work it needs.

## Minimal Implementation

- Consume the shared `src/test/backgroundFixtures.ts` helper from the manifest slice (do not fork texture stubs); write the unit tests before the implementation.
- `backgroundLayer.ts`: a small handle class `{ image, dim, setLevel, destroy, textureKey() }`; `setLevel` no-ops when the key is unchanged (idempotent), destroys nothing when the fallback is in use.
- Add the hooks on `CombatCoreScene` next to `resetRunState`/`teardownRunState`; wire the teardown call once so subclasses get it for free.
- Replace `PlayScene`'s inline rectangle with `_createBackground()` / `_setBackgroundLevel(this.waveManager.level)`; delete the now-unused local depth constant **only** if nothing else references it (report rather than silently drop dead code otherwise).
- Do not add warp/transition logic here — that is the next slice; this slice proves static per-level rendering, dimming, non-interactivity and teardown.

## Deliverables

- `src/scenes/core/backgroundLayer.ts` + `src/scenes/core/backgroundLayer.test.ts`.
- Shared hooks/constants in `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` and `src/core/constants.ts`.
- `PlayScene` initial-background wiring (no level-change swap yet).

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/core/backgroundLayer.ts` — new shared lifecycle module (create/dim/swap/destroy).
- `src/scenes/core/backgroundLayer.test.ts` — new unit tests (depth, non-interactive, fallback, teardown, idempotent swap).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — shared `_createBackground`/`_setBackgroundLevel` hooks + teardown.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — replace the inline backdrop rectangle with the shared layer.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — dim/tint/depth tuning constants; `GAME_BACKGROUND_COLOR` fallback.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — parity/duplicate-body guard (read-only unless the guard legitimately needs the new shared surface listed).

## Dependencies

- Depends on: AH-0MVSEASIM005TU95 (deterministic background manifest + fixture harness); AH-0MVSEB2WZ000MZY8 (real imagery — the layer itself works with fixture textures).
- Blocks: AH-0MVSEBW8L009O3JD (PlayScene level-change wiring); AH-0MVSEC0J0004YNJC (gym parity verification).

**Parent:** AH-0MVIB7PD50029ZY1 — Background scenes (covers parent AC3: unmistakable warp transition timed to `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS`; related to AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU "unmistakable" bar).

## Goal

As a player I want an unmistakable hyperspace "warp" when the background changes between levels, and as a developer I want that effect to be a deterministic, time-boxed, individually switchable module with a testable timeline, so level changes read as a jump through space without ever hurting readability or blocking play.

## Background

Producer answer Q2 (2026-10-25): **Option A — hyperspace-style one-shot** (converging streak overlay + radial scale distortion + brief flash/crossfade), timed to `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` (1.5 s, currently exported from `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`). Existing VFX modules show the house pattern to copy: exported tuning constants plus per-layer `*_ENABLE_*` toggles and caller-owned effect registries that are destroyed on `SHUTDOWN` (`src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts`, `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`, `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts`).

Import direction matters: `PlayScene` imports VFX modules, so a VFX module must **not** import `PlayScene`. The duration therefore moves to `src/core/constants.ts` and is re-exported from `PlayScene` for existing importers.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` moves to `src/core/constants.ts` and `PlayScene` re-exports it unchanged, so `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.ts` can derive `BACKGROUND_WARP_DURATION_SECONDS` from the same single source (no duplicated literal); all existing importers (`PlayScene.test.ts`, `SceneNavigation.test.ts`) keep compiling without edits.
2. `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.ts` exposes the full timeline as exported constants (streak phase, distortion/scale phase, flash/crossfade phase) whose phases are ordered, non-overlapping and sum to the total duration; a test asserts the sum and ordering so the effect can never outlive the transition window.
3. The effect renders three layers — converging streak overlay, radial scale distortion, brief flash/crossfade into the incoming background — each with its own `BACKGROUND_WARP_ENABLE_*` toggle (following the `ENDOFRUN_ENABLE_*` pattern) and exported magnitudes (streak count, speed, colours, scale range, flash alpha).
4. Deterministic: no `Math.random()` (or a seeded generator) — two runs from the same inputs produce byte-identical layer parameters, asserted by test. Time-boxed and observable: an `update(dt)`-style tick API (no reliance on wall-clock tweens) so a test can advance exactly `BACKGROUND_WARP_DURATION_SECONDS` and assert completion; `isComplete()` is true at the end and never before.
5. Bounded and disposable: a fixed maximum streak count (constant), all display objects inside one container, `destroy()` idempotent, and a test asserts the container/children are gone after completion and after an early `destroy()` (no leaks if the scene restarts mid-warp).
6. `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.test.ts` covers the ACs above; changed-scope tests and `tsc --noEmit` pass.

7. **Parent-AC traceability:** this slice's primary implementation is parent AC #3 — "A "warp" transition effect plays while backgrounds change — timed to the existing `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` (1.5 s) transition pause — after which the new level's background is fully shown; the effect is deterministic, time-boxed, and does not block input or wave progression." — specifically the warp effect module itself (deterministic, time-boxed, switchable); the non-blocking wiring is AH-0MVSEBW8L009O3JD; the remaining ACs of this slice are the verification and the collateral work it needs.

## Minimal Implementation

- Write the test file first against the constant/API surface you intend to ship (red → green).
- Implement the effect as Phaser `Graphics` inside a `Container` at a depth just above the background layer and below gameplay (exported depth constant); no new assets and no new dependencies.
- Choose deterministic pseudo-randomness from a small in-module LCG seeded by `(fromLevel, toLevel)` so each level pair looks slightly different but reproducible — never `Math.random()`.
- Drive animation from an explicit `update(dt)`/`tick` call (the scene's `update` feeds it) rather than `this.tweens`, matching the deterministic-boot test harness in `src/test/gameHarness.ts`.
- Keep it visually consistent with `wormholeSpawn`/`phaseShiftJuice` (violet→cyan converging lines, white flash peak).
- Do not trigger it from a scene here — the wiring slice owns the trigger; this slice ships the module plus tests.

## Deliverables

- `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.ts` — deterministic, switchable hyperspace warp effect with exported timeline.
- `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.test.ts` — timeline, determinism, completion, toggle and teardown tests.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` relocated (single source of truth).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — re-export only (no behaviour change).

**Key Files:**

- `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.ts` — new warp transition module.
- `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.test.ts` — new tests.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` + warp depth/colour constants.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — re-export `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` (no logic change).
- `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts` / `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` — patterns to mirror (read-only).
- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts` — visual-language reference (read-only).

## Dependencies

- Depends on: AH-0MVSEASIM005TU95 (deterministic background manifest — level identifiers/seeding only).
- Blocks: AH-0MVSEBW8L009O3JD (PlayScene level-change wiring).
- Related: AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU (unmistakable phase-shift/wormhole effects) — same producer bar, coordinate the visual language; this slice must not weaken that item's effect.

data.description:
**Parent:** AH-0MVIB7PD50029ZY1 — Background scenes (covers parent AC2 "changes exactly on level change", AC3 warp timing/does-not-block, AC6 integration tests).

## Goal

As a player I want the new level's background to arrive with the warp exactly when the level changes (and never mid-level), so each of the ten levels is unmistakably a different place in space while gameplay, input and wave timing are untouched.

## Background

Level changes flow `WaveManager.onEnemyDestroyed()` → `'levelCleared'` → `PlayScene._handleWaveEvent` → `_announceLevel()` + `_startTransition()` (`LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS = 1.5`). Two facts shape this slice:

1. **Two handlers.** The `levelCleared` case is duplicated in `PlayScene._handleWaveEvent` and in `PlayScene._advanceAfterTimeout()` (the wave-timer expiry path). Both must reach the background swap, so the `levelCleared` work is extracted into one helper (e.g. `_onLevelCleared()`) that both call — otherwise a level cleared by timeout skips the swap.
2. **Level is already advanced.** `WaveManager` increments `_levelIndex` *before* returning `'levelCleared'`, so `waveManager.level` during the transition is the **incoming** level: the swap target is `backgroundForLevel(waveManager.level)`, and the warp must finish no later than `transitionTimer` reaches 0 (`_onTransitionComplete()` then spawns the new wave).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. On `'levelCleared'` only — not on `'waveCleared'`, not on `'bossTriggered'`, not per wave — `PlayScene` starts the warp and swaps to `backgroundForLevel(waveManager.level)`; the same code path is reached by both the kill path (`_handleWaveEvent`) and the wave-timeout path (`_advanceAfterTimeout`), with no duplicated background logic between them.
2. The warp is created at `_startTransition()` time for a level change, advanced from the scene's own tick (not wall-clock tweens), and is complete by the time the transition ends: after ticking `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` the background's `textureKey()` equals `backgroundForLevel(newLevel)`, `isComplete()` is true, and `_onTransitionComplete()` has spawned the wave on the unchanged frame schedule.
3. Non-blocking: during the warp the player still moves, auto-fires and can teleport, and the transition/wave timer schedule is unchanged — asserted by a test that ticks half the transition while driving input and checks bullets/position, plus an assertion that `transitionRemaining()` is unaffected by the warp's presence.
4. Boss entry keeps the final level's background (documented decision: no swap and no warp on `'bossTriggered'`); asserted by test so the boss arena's backdrop is deterministic.
5. Restart/shutdown safety: starting a new run or shutting the scene down mid-warp leaves no warp container, no stale background and no leaked timer — a subsequent level change behaves normally (tested).
6. New integration suite `src/scenes/PlayScene.background.test.ts` covers ACs 1–5 and the existing `PlayScene` suites (`PlayScene.test.ts`, `PlaySceneHUD.test.ts`, `SceneNavigation.test.ts`, `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) still pass unchanged; full-suite gate is left to the dev-push gate (no ad-hoc full runs).

7. **Parent-AC traceability:** this slice's primary implementation is parent AC #6 — "Tests cover: deterministic level→background mapping, swap fires on level change (not wave), warp effect activates during the transition and completes within its duration, and the background layer does not intercept input; document updates (README, code comments, credits/attribution file with licences, GDD §3.2/§7.1 references as needed); the full project test suite passes with the new changes." — specifically the integration-tests half (swap-on-level-change-only, timing, input non-blocking, full suite); the documentation half is AH-0MVSEC4RS003KQGV; the remaining ACs of this slice are the verification and the collateral work it needs.

## Minimal Implementation

- Write `src/scenes/PlayScene.background.test.ts` first (boot via `src/test/gameHarness.ts`, drain a level to force `'levelCleared'`, use the fixture textures from the shared-layer slice).
- Extract `_onLevelCleared()` on `PlayScene`; both `_handleWaveEvent` and `_advanceAfterTimeout` call it (per the parent's "shared behaviour lives once" rule).
- In `_startTransition()`, take an optional `levelChanged` flag (or compare target level against the currently shown one) to start the warp; keep `_startTransition` otherwise identical so wave transitions are unaffected.
- Tick the warp from `update()` next to `transitionTimer`, and destroy it in `_onTransitionComplete()`/`teardownRunState()` (whichever owns cleanup) so completion and early shutdown are both safe.
- Keep the transition banner, wave timer and telemetry calls exactly as they are (no behaviour change beyond the backdrop/warp).

## Deliverables

- `PlayScene` level-change wiring: single `_onLevelCleared()` path, warp start, warp tick, cleanup.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.background.test.ts` — integration suite (swap-on-level-change-only, timing, input non-blocking, boss behaviour, restart safety).

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_handleWaveEvent`, `_advanceAfterTimeout`, `_startTransition`, `update`, `_onTransitionComplete`, `teardownRunState`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.background.test.ts` — new integration tests.

**Parent:** AH-0MVIB7PD50029ZY1 — Background scenes (covers parent AC5: gym↔game parity, shared core, documented divergence).

## Goal

As a developer I want the gyms to consume the *same* background code as the shipped game — with any divergence explicit and justified — so the parity convention in AGENTS.md holds and gym-based visual review of the new backdrop is trustworthy.

## Background

`GymFormationScene` (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`) and the direct `CombatScene` gyms (`GymWeapons`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`, `GymWeaponLeveling`) all extend the shared core, so the lifecycle hooks from the shared-layer slice are inherited for free. What is *not* settled is whether a gym should show a backdrop at all: gyms compare enemies/weapons, and a photo backdrop could distract from the comparison, yet the AGENTS.md rule says an enabled gameplay object must run the same code in both places — so the decision has to be explicit and tested either way. `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (repo-wide duplicate-body guard) enforces "one implementation".

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Gyms render through the shared layer with **no** background code of their own: `GymFormationScene` and the `CombatScene`-based gyms either enable the shared `_createBackground()` (game-identical path) or skip it via one exported, documented switch — either way the duplicate-body guard passes with no new allow-list entries and no copied draw/swap logic.
2. One explicit, documented decision is recorded on the work item and in a code comment next to the switch, with the reason (e.g. "gyms pin the level-1 backdrop so enemy silhouettes are compared against a constant backdrop, no level-change warp because gyms do not change campaign levels").
3. If gyms enable backgrounds: the gym's backdrop is a fixed representative level (`backgroundForLevel(1)`), no warp is ever triggered, and it still renders at depth ≤ −1000, non-interactive, with the same dim overlay as the game — asserted by test.
4. `src/scenes/gym/backgroundParity.test.ts` boots one formation gym and `PlayScene` with the shared fixture textures and asserts: same layer module/helper is used, identical depth/dim/non-interactive invariants, and the documented divergence (fixed level, no warp) — so a future change to one without the other fails a test.
5. All existing gym suites (`src/scenes/gym/*.test.ts`, including `GymIndex.test.ts`) pass unchanged; changed-scope gate passes.
6. Where the divergence is non-obvious, a note is added to `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 parity convention (a one-line link is enough; the docs slice owns the fuller write-up).

7. **Parent-AC traceability:** this slice's primary implementation is parent AC #5 — "Background creation/swap logic lives in the shared combat core (`src/scenes/core/`) consumed by `PlayScene` and the gyms (gym↔game parity convention in AGENTS.md); any gym divergence is documented." — specifically the gym adoption + documented-divergence half; the shared-core home is AH-0MVSEB7SA004B26C; the remaining ACs of this slice are the verification and the collateral work it needs.

## Minimal Implementation

- Write the parity test first (it can start as a red assertion that the gym's backdrop matches the game's invariants).
- Add the opt-in/opt-out switch at the shared base (`GymFormationScene`), not per gym — one decision, inherited by every formation gym; direct `CombatScene` gyms pick it up through the same base hooks.
- Reuse `src/test/backgroundFixtures.ts` from the shared-layer slice rather than adding gym-specific texture stubs.
- Record the decision in the completion comment and in the parent's Appendix so it is auditable; do not silently diverge.

## Deliverables

- Gym adoption switch (or documented opt-out) in the shared gym base, inherited by all gyms.
- `src/scenes/gym/backgroundParity.test.ts` — gym↔game background parity tests.
- One-line parity note where divergence is non-obvious.

- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` / `GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` / `GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` / `GymWeaponLeveling.ts` — direct `CombatScene` gyms (verify, edit only if they need the switch).
- `src/scenes/gym/backgroundParity.test.ts` — new parity tests.
